title: Officiating analyst Terry McAulay on the broadcast on the controversial clock ruling that allowed Michigan's Hail Mary win: "Our [on-screen] clock is in sync--is the actual stadium clock. The ball isn't even close to touching a player when it goes to zero. Now, their system--their Hawk-Eye system--apparently... had a different sync or whatever. And they came up with one second [left] when it touched the players. I don't see how that happened, assuming our clock is correct. It is clearly not touching a player--the ball is clearly still in the air when the clock goes to zero on our screen. So, you know, the Big Ten is going to have to tell a lot of us: How did they get to one second on this play?"

title: #Rockies host #STLCards tonight. They suffered kick in shins loss on Friday. But the game was stained by plate umpire Doug Eddings, who demanded that a rookie Cardinals pitcher making his debut put his cap on straight. Hunter Goodman, while hitting, asked if he could wear cap tilted, according to Eddings. The answer is yes. That is what Eddings should have said. Well Goodman said Saturday to reporters that he never brought up the tilt of the cap to Eddings, which makes Eddings look worse. Regardless, Eddings decided to conduct himself unprofessionally. Cardinals manager got tossed, understandably pissed since Eddings was out of line. Worse, there will be no punishment for the ump. That is what is so frustrating. Umpiring is hard. I get it. But no need to make it harder by making yourself the captain of the fashion police #mlbnews Curious what you all think?

title: Couple salary cap/roster notes: • The Giants are $1.3M over the cap, according to the NFLPA database. They will need to be under by Wednesday because top 51 accounting ends when the season starts. They don't need to do anything dramatic since they only need a few million to operate (at least for now). Paulson Adebo, Jevon Holland, Darius Slayton and Jon Runyan have the biggest base salaries for a restructure. It doesn't really matter who they restructure, but Schoen has typically avoided restructures on possible cap casualties, so from that group, I suspect Holland will be first up. • Schoen teased the signing of a veteran defensive lineman to the practice squad next week (don't think Jihad Ward's IG video was an announcement). They have the maximum of six veterans on their practice squad, so they'd need to cut someone from this group — WR Braxton Berrios, WR Jalin Hyatt, WR Charlie Jones, OL Darian Kinnard, DL Josh Tupou, LB Malik Harrison — to add another vet. The other option would be signing someone from that group (Berrios?) to the active roster to make room for another P-squad vet.

title: Lane Kiffin on ESPN's College GameDay on the decision to not have former NFL players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris on the roster for LSU's season opener: "That wasn't easy. As much as I feel for the players--and I believe that you fight for what you believe in, and I believe these kids have an opportunity to play just like all the other kids around the country that are winning court cases and being put on rosters--but at the same time, I'm the head coach of LSU. And I had to make a decision that is for the big picture of LSU and the LSU football program, with the uncertainties of what potentially could have come by adding them to the roster. And we couldn't get exact... what that would mean if we added them. So with that, made the decision which is [in] the best interests of the team and the university."
